BiblicalUsage: The firstripe fig is the early fruit, the first sweet thing of the season — and both prophets use it to say what Israel should have been. Hosea 9:10 says God found Israel like grapes in the wilderness and saw their fathers as the firstripe in the fig tree, before they went to Baal-peor. Micah 7:1 longs for the firstripe fruit and finds none: his soul desired the firstripe fig, and there was none to eat.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the firstripe fig is a picture of promise kept and promise lost: Israel was meant to be the first sweet fruit, and instead the tree was empty.
